summary: An empty bottle has farther to travel after a local bottling plant gives way to a regional supplier.
realLife: Oregon’s environmental agency attributed part of the decline in refillables to production consolidating far from the stores collecting empties.
inGame: The bill catalog supplies the bottle-deposit question. needs: plant location and documented backhaul route.

turns.what: An active refund still gets bottles back to the store while the bottler reassesses washing and reuse.
turns.pulledBy: Production moves away while redemption remains mandatory.
turns.writesBack: The plant’s return-route review distinguishes reuse from recycling.

turns.what: With no refund and no economical return route, the distributor stops scheduling the empty-bottle pickup.
turns.pulledBy: Freight costs exceed the value of returned empties and the obligation has ended.
turns.writesBack: The carrier’s schedule loses the pickup.
